entities.name: Gomes Eanes de Zurara
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gomes Eanes de Zurara was a Portuguese chronicler of the European Age of Discovery, a key figure associated with the expeditions of Infante D. Henrique (Henry the Navigator) and the explorations of the Atlantic Ocean.

As a member of the royal court, Zurara played a crucial role in the development of the Portuguese Empire, providing valuable insights into the lives of explorers, monarchs, and indigenous populations. His chronicles offer a unique perspective on the cultural, economic, and political transformations that shaped the Mediterranean world during the 15th century.

Zurara's work has had a lasting impact on the study of the Age of Discovery, influencing generations of historians and scholars. His chronicles continue to provide valuable primary sources for understanding the complexities of the Portuguese Empire and its legacy in the modern world.

Through his meticulous recording of events, Zurara left an indelible mark on the historical record, ensuring that the stories of these pivotal moments would be preserved for future generations to study and learn from.
